articles.title: Daredevil Has Been Unmasked More Times Than You Can Count, and He's Still Not Learning
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Daredevil just can't seem to keep his identity under wraps, as, despite the fact that he goes to inordinate lengths to keep his life as Matt Murdock and the Devil of Hell's Kitchen separate, he can't help but find himself in hot water with the public. Case in point is the newest revelation of his […]
articles.content:
No, the history of Daredevil's identity is simultaneously one of Marvel's strangest and funniest pieces of history, as Matt truly can't catch a break. Half of these reveals aren't even his fault, but somehow his reactions only get funnier over time. Today, we're diving into the newest identity reveal and Matt's various other accidental identity oustings throughout the years, going over exactly how it happens and why it works so well as a storyline for Matt specifically. After all, a guy doesn't own an “I'm Not Daredevil” Christmas sweater without having ten times more reasons than anyone should have.

Matt's newest slip of the mask came when Mister Fear launched a brand-new assault on New York City. The villain developed a drug that could completely kill fear in people's minds, and there was a drug lord bidding war to control it. However, the classic villain had also long since figured out Matt's dual life on his own, and given that he'd always been jealous of the Man Without Fear since he was outshone in law school, he decided to make things personal. He created a new strain of Fear Toxin that could target Matt's memories, dousing him with it while he was teaching his college course. Being the fearless hero he is, Matt eventually overcame this toxin, but affirmed his confidence by shouting that he was Daredevil, unaware that he was tied to his co-worker and new love interest, Sari Ellison.

Now, while this is definitely an unfortunate turn of events for everyone's favorite devil, it's actually one of his more dignified identity reveals. So, with the context of the newest take out of the way, let's dive into the hilarious number of times this has happened before, not even counting the times when Matt has chosen to do so. The first time was in Daredevil (1964) #9, but Dr. Van Eyck died in the same issue he uncovered it, funnily enough, just by putting two and two together by looking at both men's physiques. The second, and personally funniest, came in Daredevil (1964) #24, when Karen and Foggy learned Matt's identity because Spider-Man sent Matt a letter assuring him his identity was safe with him, having deduced it in issue #17.

To make it as clear as humanly possible, Spider-Man figured out Matt Murdock, a blind man, was Daredevil, and sent a handwritten letter to the place he worked explicitly saying this. There are at least three layers of stupidity to that, but what takes it from hilarious to downright side-busting is that Matt, in a fit of panic, insisted that it was actually his secret twin brother, Mike Murdock, who was Daredevil. Mike, of course, wasn't real, meaning that Matt had to occasionally take of fhis glasses and pretend to be a gangster type who could see to sell the illusion. This identity proceeded to be a cover for several years, even developing into his own person, at one point.

And trust me, that's far from the last of the shenanigans around this. Starr Saxon, a different Mister Fear, puzzled out his identity by hitting him with a pheromone trail he followed to Matt's home. A San Francisco news station put it together because Matt and Daredevil both moved to the city at the same time and had ties to Black Widow, which is probably his most embarrassing reveal, given it wasn't even anyone close to him or a villain. It was just a couple of reporters. Speaking of reporters, Ben Ulrich figured it out, and his notes were leaked by his assistant, forcing Matt to fake his death. Karen famously sold his name for drug money , which would eventually lead to the CIA learning it from Kingpin's files decades down the line.

The point is, Matt couldn't keep his identity a secret to save his life. These aren't even all of the examples, or counting when Matt gave it away willingly. He's had to employ some truly insane tactics to cover his tracks over the years, Mike Murdock notwithstanding. He's had numerous superheroic allies cover for him in his costume, from Iron Fist to Black Panther, who also figured it out on his own, FYI. Most recently, the Purple Man's children used their power to wipe Daredevil's identity from the world, letting Matt return to anonymity until about now. The cast of characters who know on both the heroic and villainous side is still kind of absurd, but it does reveal exactly why so many writers keep returning to this conflict, and why they keep undoing it.

Daredevil is, at his core, a man of juxtapositions. He's a deeply Catholic man who dresses like the Devil to inflict punishment on the unjust. He's a blind man who sees the world in more detail than anyone else could imagine. He's a lawyer who takes the law into his own hands to save others. It's that last one that draws on the inherent drama of his secret identity the most. All superheroes walk on the wrong side of the law to do what they do, but it's especially relevant to Matt because of his career and deep belief in the judicial system. Despite breaking it to be a hero, he still legitimately believes in it, and unlike someone like Spider-Man, his entire life crumbles apart at a fundamental level when that hypocrisy is dragged into the light.

If Spider-Man's identity is public, then his villains target his loved ones. If Matt's identity is public, then he's forced to defend the code of ethics he's used to justify his actions for years, all while fighting the ramifications of being a lawyer who regularly breaks the law. This singular event makes Matt's life topple like a house of cards in a wind tunnel and provides more than enough drama for an entire run between just the threat of it and the fallout. That's not even mentioning all of the inherent drama of his identity being revealed, which includes, as mentioned above, the danger it puts all of his loved ones in.

Status quo is king in comic books, yes, so whenever Daredevil's identity is revealed, you know that he's going to return to a secret identity at some point. That's just the way of the world with superhero identities. Plenty of Marvel's big names have cast their secret identities aside over the years, from Iron Man and Captain America to the X-Men, but for characters like Daredevil and Spider-Man, their masks hiding their true names are an iconic, expected part of their character. However, while the status quo is a rightfully cited reason Marvel undoes character changes and development, I truly can't say that is the main factor for Daredevil.

Simply put, the threat of Daredevil's identity being revealed is so much more interesting than a status quo where everything is public knowledge. The fallout of his reveal can sustain an entire run as he adjusts, but after the ground settles and Matt and the world have grown comfortable with his status as Daredevil, that drama is gone with nothing to replace it. Like I said, Matt is a character built around countless themes of duality and conflicting realities. Just as countless stories draw on his dual identity for drama, so do they use his faith and the violence he revels in, or the inherent tragedy of his abilities. Matt's best stories, his most impactful ones, always generate tension from one or more of these aspects of his character. Do away with any one and a vital piece of Daredevil is lost .

At the end of the day, Daredevil's secret identity is an essential aspect of his character, and stories that challenge it will always be in ample supply. The revelation to Sari is sure to put their connection in a new light, especially considering how much Matt likes her and how much she despised him for his apparent laziness and fear. If there's anything that Matt's torrid history with this secret has taught us, it's that this relationship is about to get turned up to eleven, and I cannot wait to watch it turn into an absolute dumpster fire, which is another core tenet of Daredevil's stories.

Which of Daredevil's identity reveals and recoveries is your favorite? For me, it has to be the physical letter Spider-Man sent to a blind man leading to a fake twin, because nothing written in the past sixty years of comics has come close to making me laugh that hard. Actually, scratch that, as the “I'm Not Daredevil” sweater is just insane enough to follow it up. Let us know your vote in the comments below!

articles.title: Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer,' 'Ramayana' Dominate Global Box Office as 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Crosses $100 Million
articles.summary: Johnny Depp’s return in Paramount’s "Ebenezer" won the global box office this weekend, edging out Indian powerhouse "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend" to claim the worldwide crown, while Toho’s "Godzilla Minus Zero" crossed the $100 million milestone. articles.content:
Johnny Depp 's return in Paramount's “ Ebenezer ” won the global box office this weekend, edging out Indian powerhouse “ Ramayana : Rise of a Legend” to claim the worldwide crown, while Toho's “ Godzilla Minus Zero ” crossed the $100 million milestone.

Directed by Ti West, “Ebenezer” debuted at No. 1 globally with a worldwide weekend estimate of $42 million. The dark reimagining of Charles Dickens' “A Christmas Carol” opened at the top of the North American chart with $19 million across 3,535 locations, while international audiences delivered a stronger $23 million debut across 63 markets. Audiences largely embraced Depp's turn as Ebenezer Scrooge alongside an ensemble cast featuring Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Daisy Ridley, Tramell Tillman and Ian McKellen. Exit polling yielded an “A-” CinemaScore, a 90% Verified Hot Popcornmeter rating on Rotten Tomatoes and 4.5 out of 5 stars on PostTrak (including 85% total positive and 66% definite recommend scores), with 51% of surveyed moviegoers citing Depp as their primary attendance driver. Overseas, “Ebenezer” topped the charts in several key territories, led by a No. 1 opening in the U.K. with $5.4 million from 633 locations. Other chart-topping debuts included Italy ($2 million from 365 sites), Mexico ($1.7 million from 855 sites), Spain ($1 million from 323 sites), Poland ($900,000 from 208 sites, including paid previews), Belgium ($372,000 from 74 sites, including previews) and Panama/Central America ($340,000 from 125 sites, including previews). Strong runner-up bows came from France ($2.5 million from 505 sites, including previews), Germany ($1.5 million from 512 sites), Brazil ($475,000 from 589 sites), the Netherlands ($416,000 from 103 sites) and Colombia ($262,000 from 204 sites). Elsewhere, Australia opened at No. 3 with $650,000, the U.A.E. placed fourth with $222,000 (part of a $600,000 Middle East regional bow), and Japan opened at No. 6 – ranking as the top MPA release – with $450,000. Paramount backed the launch with an extensive global marketing push anchored by Depp's surprise in-character appearance at San Diego Comic-Con (which generated over 152 million social impressions) and a trailer launch that drew more than 225 million views in seven days. International activations ranged from a winter-themed Leicester Square world premiere and London ghost tours to a Day of the Dead marigold installation in Mexico City, an end-credits song by Mylène Farmer in France, and sports integrations across the Premier League, LaLiga, Bundesliga, NFL and NBA. Hot on “Ebenezer's” heels, Namit Malhotra's “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend” retained the No. 1 international crown and took second place globally, surging to a $147.5 million worldwide cumulative gross after just 11 days in release – already making it the seventh highest-grossing Indian film of all time. Fueled by stellar word-of-mouth and brisk midweek business, the Nitesh Tiwari-directed epic enjoyed a phenomenal second-weekend hold, dropping just 34% for a $38.1 million global frame, including $32.6 million from international markets. Presented by Sony Pictures and Prime Focus Studios in association with Monster Mind Creations and DNEG, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, with a score by Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman, “Ramayana” expanded into six new markets this weekend to reach 43 territories overall. Record-breaking openings for an Indian release were notched in Indonesia ($573,000), Cambodia ($286,000) and Mexico. India remained the undisputed powerhouse with a cumulative tally of $97.2 million, buoyed by the highest second weekend in local history at INR223 crore ($23.6 million). Top-performing overseas cumes to date include the U.K. ($5.5 million), the U.A.E. ($4.7 million), Australia ($4.2 million), Thailand ($1.5 million), Malaysia ($1.4 million) and Germany ($1.1 million). The rollout continues on Nov. 19 in Brazil, Italy, Ukraine and Hungary, followed by Poland on Nov. 20 and major Latin American territories plus Czechia on Nov. 26. Meanwhile, Yamazaki Takashi's “Godzilla Minus Zero” continued its box office rampage, taking fourth place worldwide with a $15.6 million frame and pushing its global cumulative total past the $100 million mark to $104.8 million. Warner Bros.' “The Cat in the Hat” claimed third place globally with $17 million (bringing its worldwide cume to $55.8 million), while Sony's “How to Rob a Bank” rounded out the global top five with $10.2 million. In the large-format sector, local-language titles and alternative content powered Imax to a $13.7 million global weekend. “Godzilla Minus Zero” added $4.8 million across Imax screens in its sophomore frame – comprising $1.6 million in North America and $3.2 million internationally, including $1.4 million in Japan (where its local Imax total hit $6.7 million) – lifting its global Imax cume to $32 million. “Ramayana” contributed another $3 million in its second Imax weekend, with $2.6 million coming from international venues and $1.2 million from India alone (reaching $4.6 million locally), bringing its worldwide Imax tally to $12.4 million. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'The Cat in the Hat' Review: Bill Hader Leads an Animated Dr. Seuss Comedy So Overstuffed It's Like a Marvel Movie for Tots Netflix’s Genre-Bending YA Drama ‘The Body’ Is a Queer Y2K Extravaganza: TV Review

Multiplex chain Cinepolis is bringing Sala de Arte, its program dedicated to independent and international film, to Indonesia, with KlikFilm on board as curator and highlights from the ongoing Malang World Cinema set to screen in six cities across the country.

Cinepolis launched Sala de Arte in Mexico in 2012. It now runs on more than 25 screens at Cinepolis sites in Mexico, Chile, Costa Rica and Guatemala, offering a permanent slot for international and indie titles. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX

In Indonesia, KlikFilm will act as the official curator partner, selecting films for Cinepolis venues in six major cities. The companies have not yet named the cities, and said details of the rollout and screening schedules will follow soon.

The deal, announced Monday, comes two days after Malang World Cinema opened at Cinepolis Malang Town Square in East Java. The festival runs through Nov. 21 and is screening more than 200 films from 69 countries. Organizers said it has pulled in audiences from nearby cities such as Surabaya.

Demand has already prompted organizers to schedule two additional screenings of several titles. These include Palme d'Or winner “ Fjord “; “All of a Sudden,” which won best actress at Cannes this year; Cannes Grand Prize winner “Minotaur”; and “Rose,” a Silver Bear winner at the 2026 Berlinale. Also getting more showtimes are “Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie,” which took the People's Choice Award at Toronto in 2025, as well as “Wicker,” “The Samurai and the Prisoner,” “The Debut,” “All the Lovers in the Night,” “Josephine,” “La Gradiva” and “Ink.”

“This collaboration is a significant step forward for KlikFilm towards making access to world-class cinema more equitable for Indonesian audiences. Through Malang World Cinema and the upcoming expansion of Sala de Arte, we are not just bringing the finest curation of films from international festivals to the big screen, but we are also aiming to nurture a sustainable ecosystem for film appreciation that continues outside of Jakarta,” said Frederica, director of KlikFilm and executive director of Malang World Cinema. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Alejandro Aguilera Garibay, CEO of Cinepolis Cinemas Indonesia, said local viewers should be able to watch international films at the same high standard wherever they live. “Malang World Cinema opens up that opportunity, and we hope to keep the door open for a very long time. This is the spirit behind Sala de Arte – an initiative we have run in Mexico since 2012 and are now bringing to Indonesia – to ensure that a curated selection of world cinema always has a permanent place on the big screen in six cities. We are delighted to embark on this journey together with KlikFilm,” he said.

Malang World Cinema and its sister event, Bandung World Cinema, opened on Nov. 14 as the first editions of Jakarta World Cinema held outside the capital.

articles.title: 8 Standout Moments From the Governors Awards: Glenn Close Finally Gets Her Oscar, Diane Warren Pitches Olivia Wilde a Christmas Song and More
articles.summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences presented honorary Oscars to Glenn Close, Ridley Scott and Floyd Norman at the 17th Governors Awards on Sunday night at Ovation Hollywood's Ray Dolby Ballroom. articles.content:
The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences presented honorary Oscars to Glenn Close , Ridley Scott and Floyd Norman at the 17th Governors Awards on Sunday night at the Ray Dolby Ballroom at Ovation Hollywood. Killer Films co-founders Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler received the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award, becoming the first all-female producing team to take home the honor.

John Malkovich, Matt Damon, Todd Haynes and Julianne Moore served as presenters, while Tom Cruise, Pedro Pascal, Olivia Wilde, Diane Warren and Andrew Garfield were among those working a room packed with legends and Oscar hopefuls. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX

Lynette Howell Taylor, AMPAS President, set the tone, praising the honorees for "the years of determination behind them, the risks that didn't pay off, the doors that didn't open." Then she asked the crowd how many times in the last year they had found themselves referencing "Terminator 2."

Here are eight moments that stood out during the evening.

Glenn Close Finally Gets Her Oscar and Reframes Eight Losses

Close arrived as the night's sentimental center. Her eight nominations, from "The World According to Garp" (1982) to "Hillbilly Elegy" (2020), tie her with Peter O'Toole for the most acting nods without a win. The cruelest came for "The Wife" (2018), when she swept the Golden Globe, SAG and Critics Choice Awards, then lost to Olivia Colman for "The Favourite." When Malkovich finally handed her the statuette, the room erupted.

Her speech was touching and full of gratitude. Close revealed she spent the ages of 7 to 22 "under the thumb of a restrictive cult," escaping into Disney films before enrolling as a 22-year-old freshman at the College of William & Mary, where she was cast as Olivia in "Twelfth Night." "It was like water on the desert," she said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Then she addressed the losses head-on. "I have always felt that the great honor is to be in the room," Close said. "Over the past 43 years, I have been in the room eight times."

She thanked her longtime agent Kevin Huvane, who once sent flowers to her Village apartment at 10 p.m. with a note that read, "Don't let the motherfuckers get you down" and answered Howell Taylor's "Terminator 2" quip with a mission statement. "We are not machines," Close said. "We are flawed. Our imperfections are our salvation."

She closed with her daughter, Annie, who told her at age 3, "I want you. I want all of you." Said Close: "The pain of leaving is always relieved by the joy of coming home."

Diane Warren Pitches Olivia Wilde a Christmas Song

Navigating the dinner hour can be tricky, but not for someone who's done it a more than 20 times. As the contenders started walking into the room, I found myself chatting with "The Invite" star and director Olivia Wilde, who was flying back out to London tonight to finish shooting her film "Naughty," which stars Jennifer Aniston, Peter Dinklage and Regina Hall.

In the middle of it all, Diane Warren, herself a 2022 honorary Oscar recipient, walked up and introduced herself, but of course, Wilde knew who she was. After they embraced, Warren asked what she was working on and she said she was shooting a Christmas film. Warren took her shot and asked whether she could write a Christmas song for the holiday movie. Wilde said, "Absolutely," but I still don't know if I witnessed just talk or if a meeting got made.

If the Governors Awards is the unofficial start of Oscar campaigning, this year's floor made the case. Holland and Zendaya arrived together, and Holland stopped to say hello to Timothée Chalamet and Kylie Jenner. Cruise ("Digger") caught up with "Being Heumann" director Siân Heder, while "Obsession" director Curry Barker was introduced to Christopher Nolan, the DGA president, whose "The Odyssey" is one of the season's heavyweights.

"The Odyssey" star John Leguizamo crossed paths with "Michael" breakout Jaafar Jackson, and Andrew Garfield ("Artificial") mingled his way through the crowd, alongside Monica Barbaro, Yura Borisov and director Luca Guadagnino. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

John Malkovich Ranks Close's Greatest On-Screen Deaths

Close's "Dangerous Liaisons" co-star opened his tribute with a theory. "Personally, I think the mark of a great actor is how spectacularly they die on screen," Malkovich said. By that measure, Close is in a league of her own, from a falling chandelier in "Mars Attacks!" ("extra points because the chandelier was once owned by Nancy Reagan") to the bathtub finale of "Fatal Attraction."

He also had the line of the night about her range. Of her dishwashing scene in "The Big Chill," the kind of moment that would anchor most actors' highlight reels, he cracked, "For her, it's a Tuesday." And of her turn in "The Wife," he said, "She roars like the fucking lion she is."

Floyd Norman Gets His ‘Happy Ending'

Two-time Oscar winner Mahershala Ali ("Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother") presented the night's first award to Norman, 91, who joined Disney in 1956 and is widely recognized as the studio's first Black animator. "In his role as animator and story artist, Floyd was not eligible to win an Oscar for his work on these individual films," Ali said. "But tonight, he is receiving one."

Norman started as an in-betweener on "Sleeping Beauty" before Walt Disney himself spotted his gag drawings and moved him to the story team on "The Jungle Book." "Lucky for me, I didn't make Walt Disney angry," Norman said. "Apparently, I made him laugh."

His tribute package delivered a perfect Hollywood twist. When Norman was brought in to help a struggling "Monsters, Inc.," the first-time director was Pete Docter, the son of Norman's high school friend. "So I was literally working for my friend's son," Norman said.

He then delivered the evening's best kicker, recalling a critic who panned a documentary about him because his life lacked drama. "I can only remind that critic that on occasion, even movies have happy endings," he said. "And this special evening, here's my happy ending."

All five of his children were in the room to see it.

Ridley Scott Accepts for His Brother Tony

Matt Damon presented Scott's honorary Oscar with a mock grudge, rattling off "Gladiator," "Black Hawk Down" and "Alien: Covenant" as Scott films "that he did not cast me in, even though I was totally available." He then recalled walking into his first meeting with Scott planning to pass on "The Martian," fresh off playing a stranded astronaut in "Interstellar." Scott answered in five words: "No one gives a shit." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"It is about time we all saw him with an Academy Award in his hand," Damon said of the four-time nominee, who has never won competitively.

Scott, 88, accepted remotely and skipped the greatest hits. His remarks opened on the last shot of his first film, "Boy and Bicycle," made for 65 pounds in 1962 and starring his 15-year-old brother, Tony. "Both of us sharing our first film together," Scott said. "It seems just like yesterday."

He closed by accepting the honor on behalf of his brother, who died in 2012. "His great work would certainly have earned him this recognition."

Neil Patrick Harris Brings Back ‘Hedwig'

Before the Thalberg, Haynes and Moore delivered a surprise. Neil Patrick Harris, one of Broadway's Tony-winning Hedwigs, performed "The Origin of Love" from "Hedwig and the Angry Inch," one of the many films Vachon and Koffler helped bring to the screen.

Haynes followed with the story of meeting Vachon in college, when she was working the campus grill in a T-shirt spattered with grease and egg yolk. When a prankster handed her orange juice instead of an egg order, she tossed it on the grill. "Black smoke everywhere. ‘Fuck you, grill's closed,'" Haynes recalled. "She was terrifying. She was awesome."

Moore offered the budget-conscious version of the Killer Films legend. "Still Alice," which won her the Oscar, was made so cheaply that the production couldn't shoot indoors past 5 p.m. because it "couldn't afford a bigger light kit."

Christine Vachon and Pamela Koeffler Made History

Inside their clip package, there was a video of Christine Vachon telling Julianne Moore that she would one day accept the Thalberg Award and Julianne Moore says, "I'll present it to you."

That's exactly what happened, alongside her frequent collaborator Todd Haynes.

Following that lineup, Vachon admitted the honorees were nervous. "Your speeches were so incredible. We were sitting there going, ‘Oh no,'" she said. "We're just producers, guys."

Vachon noted that everyone assumes that she is the scarier half the duo. Vachon set the record straight: "But really, it is Pam you do not want to mess with." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Vachon dedicated the honor to every producer who has had to will a movie into existence, recalling a colleague in New York who told her, "I know this is really your Oscar, but it kind of feels like all of ours."

The pair also shouted out the filmmakers they worked with, the team that works at Killer Films, many of whom were in attendance and their family.

As for the statuettes themselves, Koffler noticed midway through that both women were gripping theirs for dear life.

"They're not going to take it away from us," she said, "but we are still clutching."

articles.title: Dystopian Thriller 'The Flaw' Is a Cinematic Puzzle About Totalitarianism: "Each One of Us Is a Regime"
articles.summary: David Dawson is an interrogator of The Regime, and Arthur McBain is a suspect in a cat-and-mouse game in Theophilos Papastylianos' Tallinn-premiering debut feature, based on a bestselling novel.
articles.content:
In a dark, dystopian future, the Regime decides who belongs and who doesn't. And the Regime puts the cold and calculating Interrogator on a man who becomes the Suspect to prove his guilt. He puts a ruthless plan of psychological manipulation into action. But could there be a shortcoming in the master plan?

The dystopian thriller The Flaw , a Greece–Latvia co-production, is based on Antonis Samarakis' novel of the same name, which is a modern Greek classic and bestseller. It is also writer-director Theophilos Papastylianos' ( Algorhythm , Showtime ) feature debut, and it is about to get its world premiere, appropriately in the Baltics. The film will debut in the Baltic Film Competition of the 30th edition of Estonia's Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) on Wednesday, Nov. 18. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies A Man Has Just Retired, But the Government Insists He Is Dead. Welcome to 'When I Existed'! (Exclusive Trailer, Plus Chat With the Directors) Lifestyle Soho House Creator Nick Jones Is Reinventing the Hotel -- Again

British talent leads The Flaw , with David Dawson, who plays Derek Jarman in Elsinore , portraying the Interrogator, and Arthur McBain ( After the Flood , Napoleon ) playing the Suspect. Also part of the ensemble cast are Ralf Little, Angela Brouskou, Lyne Renée, Sarah Akokhia and Georgia Small. Thodoris Zacharakis is the cinematographer, while Yannis Chalkiadakis is the editor. Produced by Panos Papahadzis and Papastylianos, the co-producers are Alise Rogule and Lina Yannopoulou. Jacques Kruger is the sales agent.

Papastylianos talked to THR ahead of the film's premiere about just how timely and urgent The Flaw feels, its cast and visuals, and why the film is like one giant puzzle.

How did you approach adapting the novel after you read it? It was my second time reading the book, and it was a revelation for me because the perspective was completely different. I wasn't reading it as a teenager, like the first time. Now, I was reading it as a director. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The most important part when I wrote the script was to take a step back and say, “Okay, this is an amazing idea, but the film is going to be released in five to seven years. Is it going to be amazing in seven years?”

That said, the film feels scarily timely.

It was instinct because I was seeing how the whole world was progressing and how society was changing. I felt this book was timeless, and as the years go by, it's going to become more up to date all the time.

The weird thing for me is that, in a sense, I'm happy that the film is up to date. But on the other hand, I'm sad because that means our society and the world are taking a very dramatic shift towards a place that is not good.

Can you talk a bit about the themes of totalitarianism and beyond that The Flaw explores?

For me, the totalitarian regimes and everything is just the first level. I wanted the film to act as a strong allegory. You have the regimes, the governments, or society, that is all around us. But I actually think that each one of us is a regime by himself.

We perceive the world through our own eyes and our own perspective, and through our own prejudice. So, by definition, we are a regime by ourselves. Imagine a hunter walking in the woods, and all of a sudden, he sees a deer. So he lifts up his rifle and looks through the scope. At that moment, he sees prey. If he could just take a moment and lower the scope, he would see a deer again. And I think it's the same thing with people. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

We meet somebody, and we judge them right off the bat – their sexual orientation, [how they look], how political or non-political they are. During COVID, for example, there were two groups of people: the anti-vaccine and the vaccine people, but nothing in the middle. But for me, that's the interesting thing: people meet in the middle.

The two protagonists in The Flaw go through an evolution, but I didn't fully notice it until the end…

What we were aiming for was a slow change that the characters go through. We wanted to be so slow that you realize that the characters you've been seeing from the beginning, all of a sudden, at the end, are completely different characters.

The film has some spectacular-looking buildings. How did you think about locations?

We shot in Greece, and we also shot in Riga in Latvia. Riga was a very important part of the whole process in order to get that feeling of brutalism and all this dark, timeless sensation.

But then we had to combine Greece with Riga, and that was a challenge, so we could get a timeless space and locations where you don't know they were actually shot in two different countries. The production design team did an amazing job. And lighting and framing were very important for us. I believe that when we shoot, we make conscious choices that actually affect people's subconscious.

So every shot is there for a reason. Every close-up is there for a reason. We choose what we want to show or what we don't want to show the audience. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The Flaw features Greece and Latvia as locations. But the two lead characters are played by British guys. Tell me a bit about the casting decisions.

It was amazing to work with all these guys. They are amazing professionals. I actually sent paintings, portraits, to the casting director. And I said, “Look, this is the energy that I'm looking for as a character.” I used a lot of [Amedeo] Modigliani in terms of the paintings that I sent, because he has this energy and these figures that are surreal, but at the same time, they're actual people.

My process with the actors once they know the scenes is this. When they ask me what I think about a scene and the characters, I always say to them, “I don't have anything to say to you. You know the script. You know the scenes. You know your character. Just present your approach.” You need to give actors space so they can breathe on their own.

Tell me a bit about Greek theater and film actress Angela Brouskou and her role of the “Head”?

What we were aiming at was that the Head should not be a natural person but should be on the edge of becoming an idea. She represents the Regime. She is the Regime. So you have a character, but the way she's depicted, sometimes you think that she is a non-character. It's like she's becoming the idea of the regime. She becomes a persona that turns into an idea.

[Warning: This question and answer contains what may be considered a spoiler.] David and Arthur have such a fascinating dynamic and chemistry that keeps shifting. How did you approach their characters' relationship? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For me there was a key thing. One is the alter ego of the other. So, our big challenge was to [make sure you] see hidden qualities that slowly start coming out more and more. And before the shoot, I showed them the paintings, the portraits, that [I had shared with the casting team]. And I also gave them two pieces of music they could listen to. I truly believe that our work has a lot to do with the energy of the people.

I am glad you mentioned music because that seems to play into the characters and story of The Flaw very strongly…

Yes, I got Dimitris Fessas, the composer, and we worked a lot with him. We wanted to have these rough-edged, train-like pieces. We wanted to use a lot of the electric guitar combined with violins or violas, and then he actually used a traditional Greek instrument called the Cretan lyra. There are actually scenes where the Cretan lyra is having this discussion with the electric guitar. And then a violin steps in, and the whole sensation is a little bit out of this world – in a good sense.

We created the melody of the Interrogator and the melody of the Suspect, but in the end, these two melodies have to interweave. The sound design was also an important [element of that]. We paid so much attention to every detail, especially sound-wise.

Talking to you makes me understand why I experienced The Flaw as pieces of a puzzle slowly emerging and a bigger picture coming into view.

I think that's the best way to describe it. That's amazing how you put it. Yeah, the whole film is pieces of a puzzle that have to come together.

articles.content:
Glenn Close is leaning into the campy side of her work.

The legendary actress joked with me Sunday night on the red carpet at the Governors Awards in Hollywood that so much of her career has been for her LGBTQ fans.

"My career is to create characters for gay Halloween parades," she said, smiling.

Close's latest addition to her gay Halloween parade collection is Drusilla Sickle in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." Her outlandish look, which she designed, is sure to be popular next Halloween. "It's one of the characters like Cruella, like Norma Desmond, the character isn't there until you're in full drag," she said. "It's really fun." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Jo Koy on ‘Blue in the Face,’ Steven Spielberg, Biggie’s Mom and Learning What His Name Really Means at Long John Silver’s 'I Swear' Star Robert Aramayo on the BAFTA N-Word Incident That Overshadowed the Movie and the ‘X-Men’ Wolverine Pitch He Keeps Hearing

articles.title: 'The Gospel of Christmas' Review: Tyler Perry's Churchy Musical Drama Does a Threadbare Job of Getting Into the Spirit
articles.summary: "The Gospel of Christmas" is a straight-up drama of faith (losing it, testing it, regaining it), which would be fine if the film weren’t wrapped around a family saga so rickety and threadbare that it’s like watching a Sunday sermon stretched out to movie form.
articles.content:
As an intermittent Tyler Perry fan, I was eager to see what a Tyler Perry Christmas movie would look like. That's partly because I love Christmas movies, but also because it seemed a natural for his wheelhouse. Did I want to hear Madea, in her sinfully irreverent but pious way, go off on Christmas? Hell, yes. I also wanted to see Tyler Perry's idea of making merry.

But Perry's “ The Gospel of Christmas ” turns out to be as earnest and generically reverential as its title. There is no Madea in it; there is no Tyler Perry performance as any other nasty relative; and there is very little of his shameless but diverting soap-opera extravagance. “The Gospel of Christmas” is a straight-up drama of faith (losing it, testing it, regaining it), which would be fine if the film weren't wrapped around a family saga so rickety and threadbare it's like watching a Sunday sermon padded out to movie form. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Peacock Sets 'Love Trapped: The Case of Laura Owens' Documentary About 'Bachelor' Star Clayton Echard Scam

One reason “The Gospel of Christmas” has such a weirdly abstract flavor is that it's a musical, filled with churchy soul and gospel numbers designed to carry the action along. Some of the songs are quite lovely, and a couple of them are pop-gospel rousers, yet their mood is so at odds with the rest of the film that they almost seem part of another movie. The songs don't make “The Gospel of Christmas” any less sodden — they just break up the soddenness like commercials.

The film's star, Durrell “Tank” Babbs, is a good actor, but the role Perry has written for him calls on him to mope, wallow in self-pity, get angry and irritated, and then mope some more. It's as if we were watching George Bailey from “It's a Wonderful Life” at his most hopeless moment, only stretched out to 90 minutes. Babbs' Isaac Jefferson is a former bad-boy pop singer who was once famous (his biggest hit: “Gimme Them Panties”), but his career hit the skids 20 years ago. How did that happen? We're not sure. Nothing in “The Gospel of Christmas” is filled in in a convincing way. The film plays like a Christmas “parable” because it's so stripped of detail. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

On his deathbed, Isaac's clergyman father asks Isaac to take over the Baptist church of his great-grandfather, which is located in New York City. Isaac, the prodigal son, has no desire to become a pastor. But he feels like he can't turn his father down. So he and his wife, Rebecca (Fantasia Barrino), and their two sons — Jacob (Mason Douglas), surly and tall, and Esau (Eric Wiltz), who's about 10 and does not speak — move from Georgia to Perry's studio-set version of the big bad city, which looks even stagier than the New York of “Eyes Wide Shut.” The church, a stone edifice, is an impressive chunk of real estate, but when Isaac gets into the office he sees a pile of foreclosure letters. The church is five months behind on rent, and with penalties and taxes they'll need to come up with $58,000 to keep it going.

That's quite a demand, but Isaac's real burden is that he's forgotten how to pray; he's forgotten how to believe. The movie is all about his coming to see the light, but you wish it happened in a more flowing, less contrived way. “The Gospel of Christmas” has a chorus of angels, who give the movie its only hint of levity. It's got a villain, Mr. Ehtami Lived, a pawn-shop purveyor who represents Temptation — though Ricco Ross, who plays him, is a subtle enough actor to give him more dimension than anyone else in the movie. There's a plot twist that's a real whopper, as Isaac, out of nowhere, gets offered $3 million to do a concert tour — an offer, his whole family realizes, that's coming straight from the devil, though the audience for his kick-off concert is so pumped that all I could think was, "Why did his career jump the track?" Isaac, of course, gets his faith groove back, and I suppose you could say that “The Gospel of Christmas” is more of a Christmas movie than most Christmas movies, since it's really about…believing in Jesus. If only it were easier to believe the story it's telling.

articles.title: This Classic Cartoon Crossover Still Blows My Mind 39 Years Later, Even If It Made Perfect Sense
articles.summary: Hanna-Barbera, creator of the classic cartoons Yogi Bear, The Flintstones, The Jetsons, Scooby-Doo, and many others, created ten made-for-television movies in the late 1980s. Titled the Hanna-Barbera Superstars 10, these films centered around fan-favorite characters and even featured a crossover between The Jetsons and The Flintstones. As two main properties under the Hanna-Barbera umbrella, the […]
articles.content:
The Jetsons Meet the Flintstones came out on November 15, 1987, and it was released on VHS four times from 1988 up to 2001. It was also released on DVD in June 2011. The film followed fan-favorite characters from both franchises, but, despite advertising for the film, it didn’t include The Flintstones characters Orbitty, Pebbles, and Bamm-Bamm. The Jetsons Meet the Flintstones also marked a return to previous form, with the film being the first Jetsons project to use traditional cels for animation since “The Vacation” in The Jetsons.

Even 39 years later, the film is still a little mind-blowing, even while it makes perfect sense. The Jetsons and The Flintstones were both cartoons centered around families navigating a world unfamiliar to viewers. While The Flintstones has had a film since , The Jetsons hasn’t, so perhaps it’s the combination of the two that The Jetsons needs to work for a film format. The combination allows for humor not only about cavemen but also about the future, all while being shown to an audience in the present. Check out the iconic first meeting below!

A Crossover Made Possible by Time Travel A crossover between The Flintstones and The Jetsons was always going to involve time travel. Either it would be time travel putting them into each other’s path, or the creators would have to reveal that they weren’t as far apart in time as they first appeared. The main question to answer then was if the Flintstones were going forward in time, or if the Jetsons were going to go back. Over the course of the film’s ninety-two-minute runtime, the answer would be both.

At first, the Jetsons go back in time. Elroy Jetson manages to create a time travel machine, and the Jetson family decides they are due for a relaxing vacation. The time travel machine takes them to the camping park where the Flintstones have decided to take a holiday of their own. The two families become friends with the Jetsons sharing their futuristic gadgets with the Flintstones. In hopes of getting his job back — Fred lost it earlier in the film after being caught gambling by his boss — Fred uses the Jetsons’ tech to help Mr. Slate’s chances in a competition at the company picnic. Mr. Slate agrees to give Fred his job back if he can secure a victory for Mr. Slate — unfortunately, even with a technological advantage, Mr. Slate still ends up losing, and fires Fred again.

During the Jetsons’ absence, Henry Orbit and Rosie the Robot Maid assemble a device to bring them back. The device locks onto the Flintstones instead, though, and brings the prehistoric cavemen into the future, stranding the Jetsons in the past. George Jetson manages to get himself a job with Mr. Slate, becoming his partner, and quickly becomes famous. Newly rich, the Jetsons buy multiple local businesses in town. In the future, the Jetsons’ robot helps manage to fix the time machine and Rosie the Robo Maid is sent back in time to retrieve her family. The Jetsons are brought back to the future, and the film ends with the Flintstones being sent back to their past.

In the 1990s, two video games would take inspiration from The Jetsons Meet the Flintstones , not only proving the success of the crossover but also continued interest in the conceit of the film. In 1991, NES released The Flintstones: The Rescue of Dino & Hoppy. To rescue the kidnapped pets, Fred Flintstone must reassemble a time machine and travel to the future. As part of the future stage, Fred Flintstone does end up running into George Jetson. In 1994, “Flintstones/Jetsons Time Warp” was released in Europe and the game followed a similar plot from the movie. In Flintstones/Jetsons Time Warp , a time machine sends Fred Flintstone to the future and George Jetson to the past.

In 1995, The Flintstones Meet the Jetsons was featured in an episode of The Simpsons . In “A Star is Burns”, an episode from The Simpsons’ sixth season, Bart Simpson is seen watching The Flintstones Meet the Jetsons. As he watches, he says he can “smell another cheap cartoon crossover”. It refers both to the film and to the crossover about to happen in the episode of The Simpsons.

What cartoon crossovers stand out as having aged well versus having gone the way of cliché? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Netflix's Godzilla Anime Hit Really Needs a Season 2
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Bones / Orange Godzilla has been on the rise in popularity over several decades, rampaging its way to new heights across countless media, including Hollywood and Japanese movies, TV shows, anime series, video games, comics, and more. However, one of its most underrated projects is the 2021 Netflix anime, Godzilla Singular Point, which was produced by Studio Bones and […]
articles.content:
The anime followed the story of Yun Arikawa and his partner, Haberu Katou, who were on a mission to investigate a house rumored to be haunted. However, they never expected to stumble into a mystery that threw the entire planet into chaos. The anime was released in 2021 and immediately drew fans' attention for its exceptional story. Not to mention that it even won the anime won the 53rd Seiun Award in the Best Media category in 2022. However, even though more than five years have passed since the anime's debut, there has been no confirmation of a sequel season.

During the time of its production, it was evident that the production studios had plans for returning with the series, but things changed after the release. Although the main conflict of the first season was resolved with Jet Jaguar defeating Godzilla, things got interesting in the post-credits scene. The post-credits scene not only teases major future threats, but it also confirms that Goro Ashihara, the genius scientist believed to be dead or vanished, is actually in a secret facility constructing a Mechagodzilla.

The man-made monster is created using the original Godzilla skeleton and red dust/Archetype technology, confirming that humanity and the surviving forces will face a new and more powerful antagonist than ever. However, even after a cliffhanger, it appears the studios have ditched the series, considering it wasn't a groundbreaking commercial hit. Japanese fans loved the series, as evidenced by the fact that it topped Netflix charts and overperformed in merchandising sales on top of winning awards.

However, the reception in the West wasn't too positive, considering many found the constant kaiju fights confusing. Not to mention that the series leaned too much into the heavy scientific exposition without resolving many questions. While the series hasn't been officially cancelled yet, there's no guarantee that the anime will ever return with a sequel, especially after more than five years of silence from the animation studios. It was released as a collaborative project between Studio Bones and Studio Orange, both of which are heavily occupied with their multiple other anime projects.

Do you think Godzilla Singular Point deserves a second season? What would you like to see in the anime if it returns? Share your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: 5 Spider-Man Villains Who Have Completely Disappeared & Deserve a Comeback Today
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Spider-Man has one of the best rogues' galleries in all of comics, but there are so many great villains that many promising ones are overshadowed and completely disappear without a trace. Spider-Man has fought villains as famous as Doctor Octopus, the Green Goblin, Carnage, Kraven, and many more, and this makes it easy for newer […]
articles.content:
From villains who almost killed Spider-Man in one of the biggest Marvel crossovers of all time to two villains who went on to find redemption, only to disappear shortly thereafter, these are the best candidates for comebacks today. One of these villains was even hinted at before Spider-Man: Brand New Day came out , but she never appeared in the movie.

Hobie Brown debuted as the Prowler in The Amazing Spider-Man #78 (1969) by Stan Lee and John Buscema. Hobie was a bright but angry Bronx teen fired from his window-washing job. He then built the Prowler gear to steal until Spider-Man unmasked him on a rooftop and urged him to turn his life around. He later became an ally of Spider-Man. Hobie finally became the Hornet in King in Black: Planet of the Symbiotes #2 (2021). As the Hornet, he repels symbiotes by broadcasting high-frequency sound through hacked Stark phones.

The Hornet suit activates from a button on the collar and gives him shoulder-mounted wings plus wrist gauntlets like his old Prowler bracelets. The last time anyone saw Hobie was in 2022, when the Beyond Corporation bought his company, Fairgray, and later offered him a job. Hobie has appeared in Spider-Man: The Animated Series , The Spectacular Spider-Man , and the 2017 Spider-Man series.

Regent debuted in Amazing Spider-Man: Renew Your Vows #1 (2015), a “Secret Wars” tie-in by Dan Slott and Adam Kubert. In that Battleworld story, Regent rules New York, captures heroes, and drains their powers through a mechanism that holds them. He even rebuilt the Sinister Six to hunt Spider-Man. To show his true power, he used Nightcrawler's powers to remove the Hulk piece by piece, one of the best moments in the entire story.

His threat is what forces Peter Parker to retire as Spider-Man to protect his wife and daughter Annie, which is the emotional core of Renew Your Vows . It ended up being Annie who helped beat him with an arrowhead infused with her inhibitor bracelet. While that was the alternate “Secret Wars” world, Marvel brought a main-universe Augustus Roman into The Amazing Spider-Man #12-15 (2016) by Dan Slott and Giuseppe Camuncoli. His wife and child died during an Avengers battle, which drives his plan to contain superheroes. He should be more than a stereotypical bad guy, and he deserves a much bigger story.

Ollie Osnick first appeared as Kid Ock in Peter Parker, the Spectacular Spider-Man #72 (1982) by Bill Mantlo and Ed Hannigan. Ollie is part of a supervillain club, but he is mocked by the other members. To prove himself, he builds imitation Octopus arms and robs a toy store. Spider-Man destroys the arms, but when he realizes Ollie is a kid, he takes him away before the police arrive. The real Doc Ock later mocks the discarded gear.

He returned as Spider-Kid in The Amazing Spider-Man #263 (1985), and he tries to become Spider-Man's sidekick. He even went on to form the Misfits alongside Frog-Man and Toad. He went dark as the Steel Spider in Spider-Man Unlimited #5 (1994). After his girlfriend Jane was shot by a stray bullet, he modified his Spider-Kid suit and beat the gang member responsible until police arrived. He refused to register in “Civil War,” so Venom bit off his arm, Radioactive Man cauterized his wound, and he was imprisoned in the Negative Zone. Captain America released him, and he deserves a comeback to see what this did to him mentally.

Spider-Queen was the catalyst in one of Spider-Man's biggest crossovers of the 21st century, “Spider-Island.” Adriana “Ana” Soria debuted in The Spectacular Spider-Man #15 (2004) by Paul Jenkins and Michael Ryan. She was a member of the women's auxiliary corps in World War II. She was drafted into a Marine super-soldier program, survived radiation exposure at Bikini Atoll when most subjects died, and was confined in a military asylum before activating a dormant insect gene. This gave her telekinesis and a sonic scream, and she can control anyone with the insect gene.

Her kiss infected Peter Parker and began his slow transformation into an insectoid monster. She returned as the backer of the Jackal in “Spider-Island,” where infected bedbugs gave New Yorkers spider-powers. She killed the Jackal and grew into a giant spider before Kaine killed her. The Jackal she killed was a clone, and the real Jackal, disguised as Damage Control, harvested marrow from her body for future cloning. This gives Marvel a perfect reason to bring the Spider-Queen back.

If there is one Spider-Man villain who deserves to return, and who is missed greatly, it is Doppelganger. The Spider-Man Doppelganger debuted in The Infinity War #1 (1992) by Jim Starlin and Ron Lim. He was one of an army of evil doubles of Earth's heroes made by the Magus and the entity Anthropomorpho. In the end, he is a bloodthirsty, nearly mindless, yet exact duplicate of the real Spider-Man.

Doppelganger has six arms, talons, and organic spinnerets that fire razor-sharp webbing. He can also lift around 65 tons compared with Spider-Man's roughly 10-ton limit. He seemed to die early, impaled on a fence post in a fight with Spider-Man, Hobgoblin, and Demogoblin, until Demogoblin revived him with magic and made him a sidekick. He appeared in “Maximum Carnage” as Shriek's pet and then again in Carnage #1 (2010). He last appeared in Extreme Carnage: Scream #1 (2021), other than a cameo while he was in prison in Chasm: Curse of Kaine #2. He has died more than once and remains a fan-favorite villain.

What Spider-Man villain do you consider to be underrated, and who deserves a comeback? Let us know your favorites in the comments below.

articles.title: 5 Perfect '90s Sci-Fi TV Shows That Only Got Better Every Season
articles.summary: Image courtesy of Warner Bros. Television Television series are always a bit of a challenge. It isn’t just making a good season that gets audiences invested. It goes further because you have to build a story that works season after season to keep the momentum going. This is especially true when it comes to sci-fi. Shows in the sci-fi genre often […]
articles.content:
Here are five sci-fi series from the 1990s that are not only great, but they got better with each season. These are the shows that we keep coming back to all these years later because of how good they are, but also for how they built on themselves to deliver from start to finish.

Sure, Star Trek: The Next Generation isn’t the first Star Trek series, but it is in many ways the absolutely definitive one. The series was solid from the start, debuting in 1987, but it was the third season that really saw the series make a massive leap and after that, it was only better from there. The first two seasons of The Next Generation were, admittedly, a little campier than the others, but they also had a lot of heavy lifting to do. They had to establish this iteration of the franchise, the characters, and really get us invested but starting in Season 3, the stories became even more evolved, the characters more richly developed, and saw not only the series reach its full potential every season after that but also expanded the Star Trek universe in a way that made it one of the most beloved IP in not just sci-fi but entertainment on the whole. The Next Generation is an example of a series that never diminished in quality, which is rare.

I feel like we don’t give Babylon 5 nearly the appreciation it deserves, but the series, which ran from 1993 to 1998, is one of the genuinely great sci-fi series of all time and a huge part of that comes down to how it was planned. Babylon 5 , unlike most sci-fi series of its era, started with a complete five-year plan. Series creator J. Michael Straczynski knew going into the very first episode where he wanted things to go. This meant that there was a path forward for each story, each character, each arc. The first season set things up, specifically the politics and organization of the world and lore and then was able to use that basis to create something that had not only thorough storytelling, but rich emotional development. The result is a series that simply got better and better because it knew where it was going. There’s really not been anything quite like it since.

This one is a little tricky. The X-Files is undoubtedly one of the best sci-fi series ever made and you can definitely say that it’s a series that did get better season over season, but not consistently. The X-Files ran for 9 seasons in its original run between 12993 and 2002, but the series varies wildly. Seasons 1 through 5 are considered the best of the series and if you look just at those five seasons, it’s definitely a situation where the show just got better and better. The first season of The X-Files set the stage but by the time you get to Season 3, you have a series that has built on its conspiracies as well as the monster of the week format to deliver something intriguing. Even now, if you ask a fan about the best episodes of the series, they’re going to be found here. Things shift by the time we get to the sixth season — there are some production changes and the conspiracy elements of the show start to get a little unfocused here — and the whole thing declines after that, but those first five seasons just kept building on each other making The X-Files a classic.

I admit that this one is a little bit of an outside choice. When most people think about 3rd Rock From the Sun , they think of it as simply a sitcom and technically that is correct. The NBC series, which ran from 1996 to 2001, is in fact a sitcom and a popular one. But it’s also a sci-fi sit come, which is admittedly a little rare. If you’re not familiar, 3rd Rock From the Sun follows four extraterrestrials who come to Earth as part of a research expedition and, to carry this out, they pose as a normal human family in Ohio. Clearly the idea of aliens trying to be human is where the humor comes in. But while it’s funny, the series is also sci-fi (aliens coming to Earth kind of seals that.) From season to season, it’s the humor that just keeps getting better, as well as the different character arcs that see the aliens growing ever more connected to and entangled with human life and emotions. The cast also just keeps getting better each season in their roles.

The original Quantum Leap is one of those classic sci-fi series that pretty much everyone remembers because it had a pretty unique premise: Dr. Sam Beckett finds a way to time travel and tests it on himself. However, it doesn’t quite work as expected and Sam’s consciousness “leaps” from time to time, inhabiting the bodies of people where he has the opportunity to fix events in the pass, all on the hope that he will eventually leap back home to his own time. While the series starts out focused on the correcting of the past, each season improved on that first season and premise by getting more and more into the overall mythology of these leaps. As the seasons went on, the series also started taking on real social issues and widening the world with real threats not only to Sam but history as well. The show built on it’s sort of gimmicky premise to get viewers hooked in what was ultimately a deeply emotional and human story — and we’re never getting over the endin g.

What ‘90s sci-fi series do you feel like got better season after season? Let us know in the comments.

articles.content:
The Oscar-nominated directors of “ Writing With Fire ,” Rintu Thomas and Sushmit Ghosh, have unveiled the fourth cohort of the Himalayan Story Lab , their year-long fellowship for documentary filmmakers from the South Asian Himalayas.

Eight filmmakers will develop six documentaries through the 2026–27 edition, with stories drawn from Kashmir, Ladakh, Uttarakhand, Assam, Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh and Nepal. Cannes Grand Prix winner Payal Kapadia (“All We Imagine as Light”), Sundance winner and Oscar nominee Shaunak Sen (“All That Breathes”), veteran documentarian Sanjay Kak and French editor Yael Bitton are confirmed as mentors. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories U2 Gets On Its Boots for First All-New Full-Length Record in Nine Years, 'Carnaval de Luz,' With More Callbacks to Band's '90s Peaks Than '80s Glories: Album Review Dolly Parton's Last Recorded Song Released: Listen to Her Passionate Performance on U2's 'Torn'

The lab launched in 2023 with just three fellows and has since backed 25 filmmakers from India and Nepal. Thomas and Ghosh, whose “Writing With Fire” won two awards at Sundance, set it up because filmmakers based far from the region's main production hubs rarely get long-term creative guidance, producing help or a way into the international industry.

The model pairs three residential workshops with year-round mentorship on both the creative and producing sides, delivered by documentary directors, producers and editors working in India and overseas. articles.title: Every '80s Kid Remembers Where They Saw This Iconic Movie, But They All Forgot the Character's Origin Story
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of MGM The 1980s were full of incredible slasher movies, but one movie changed everything about the genre, and most people don't remember how it all started. The slashers began in the 1970s, with films like Black Christmas and Halloween leading the way to the 1980s, where the titles began to multiply. Friday the 13th became one […]
articles.content:
However, while everyone remembers Chucky as a murderous, psychotic toy voiced by Brad Dourif, not as many people remember how he got that way. This was the main plot of the first Child's Play movie , though, and it was the story of Charles Lee Ray that drove the story and has been embedded in everything Chucky has done since.

Child's Play Is a Voodoo Possession Movie at Heart Image Courtesy of MGM The original Child's Play movie started with a scene that seems almost out of place for people who only know the franchise for Chucky himself. That movie began with a fugitive serial killer named Charles Lee Ray on the run from the police. He was known as the Lakeshore Strangler in Chicago, and he was being pursued by a police detective named Mike Norris. Charles' partner, Eddie Caputo, ran from the scene, with Mike's partner chasing him. Meanwhile, Charles ran into a toy store to hide out.

While in the toy store, Mike Norris shot Charles Lee Ray. While Charles was lying on the floor and dying, he invoked the power of Damballa and cast a voodoo spell to transfer his soul into a nearby Good Guy talking doll. After this, lightning strikes the store, causing an explosion. Norris finds Charles' lifeless body on the floor with the Good Guy doll sitting next to him. This then leads to the scene where Karen Barclay buys her six-year-old son Andy a Good Guy doll for his birthday, and it is the one possessed by Charles Lee Ray.

Breaking this down, Damballa is a real-life spirit, considered among the most important of all loa, which are spirits from the West African Vodun, Haitian Voodoo, and other African diaspora religious traditions. He is often portrayed as a giant white or black serpent, and this legend dates back hundreds of years. What is interesting here is that Damballa is a benevolent creator spirit, and the movie only borrowed his name to add the voodoo aspects, inverting his peaceful nature into a vehicle for a serial killer.

When looking back on Child's Play , it is easy to remember that Chucky was tormenting six-year-old Andy and his single mother, and Mike Norris showed up to help them. However, while that was the final plot, it wasn't what Chucky was really up to in the movie. Instead, Chucky was out killing people that he knew when he was still human. He killed the criminal who ran and abandoned him at the toy store, and it isn't until young Andy is accused of the murders that Norris realizes what is going on and helps take out Chucky.

While Damballa's name was used in the voodoo spell that Charles Lee Ray called on to help transport his soul into the Good Guy doll, the spirit was not really an evil presence. That didn't stop the third season of Chucky from bringing the spirit back to the franchise. The spirit was brought back in Bride of Chucky , when Tiffany summons Damballa to resurrect Chucky, and then Chucky uses the chant again in Cult of Chucky . Damballa himself appears in the season as a god of death and as Chucky's heavenly judge. In Chucky Season 3, Episode 7, a dead Chucky ends up in the spirit realm and meets the real Damballa.

Damballa then takes the form of Chucky and has Charles Lee Ray appear as himself to touch on his narcissism. While Chucky brags about all his kills as a slasher villain, including that of a U.S. president, Damballa dismisses him, saying that he was just coasting along and was cheating on him with other gods. It really brought the voodoo and religious symbolism to the forefront. By the time they are done, Damballa offers Chucky one last chance before sending him to Hell. He tells Chucky to harness the blood spilled in the White House with originality. Chucky returned to life, and he escaped at the end of the season, which ended up being the show's finale.

articles.content:
But thankfully the future has been set in place not long after. Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World- fans thankfully didn’t have to wait too long to find out whether or not the anime would be continuing as it has now been officially announced that the anime is now in production on Season 5. During a special event in Japan this weekend to help celebrate the 10th anniversary of the TV anime’s original debut, Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World- has now confirmed Season 5 is in the works with the first look at the coming episodes.

Since the Fall 2026 anime series have already been revealed, the sequel will only be released next year. The announcement was made earlier this month with a promotional video that shares a brief glimpse at everything that has happened in the anime so far. Instead of sharing spoilers on what to expect from the sequel, the teaser only confirms the sequel without a lot of details. While fans await updates on the anime, at the very least, it’s guaranteed that the sequel will land on Crunchyroll.

It’s the primary streaming home for the series, where you can catch up with all the seasons. The fourth season has been running for two cours, and it was scheduled for 19 episodes. While the English dub was released simultaneously with the subbed episodes for the first cour, the schedule changed when the anime returned from hiatus. Instead of typically dividing the fourth season into two parts, the anime went on a few weeks of hiatus after the Loss Arc ended in Episode 11.

With Rem now fully back in the picture, but seemingly without any of her memories of her time with Subaru, the two of them need to find a connection once more in this new circumstance. They have been separated from everyone else with that cliffhanger. While Season 4 was working its way through the Recapture Arc with its new episodes airing this Summer, but the latest episode just had one of its biggest shocks yet with the “return” of Rem for the first time in ten years.

She had gone into a coma at the end of the first season following Gluttony’s attack, and she makes a special return to get Subaru ready to get back into the action. But with Gluttony now moving into action, there’s a hope that Rem’s full return won’t be too far along from this point. She was brought to the tower with the hope of figuring out how to bring her back from her coma, and her existence within this mysterious space proves that she’s still out there for Subaru and the others to find.

With Subaru overcoming all of the challenges of the Loss and Recapture Arcs seen in the fourth season, Rem has finally woken up from her coma and is set to be an active part in the series once more.On congratulating the anime franchise for making it to its fifth season, original series creator Tappei Nagatsuki teased a bit of the brutal journey that Subaru is about to embark on in Season 5. As for what’s coming, it turns out Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World- is about to get even more intense than what happened before , “The sixth arc covered in Season 4 has been called one of the most difficult parts of Re:ZERO , but don’t worry!

The journey through the seventh arc is every bit as brutal, with the difficulty cranked all the way up to inferno.” “The story continues with the same reassuringly heart-breaking design you’ve come to expect—yes, ‘heart-breaking’ is intentional!” Nagatsuki continues to tease about the coming season. “Of course, it won’t all be hardship. There will also be plenty of new encounters, exciting developments, and scenes I can’t wait to see—and show you—in anime form!” With all sorts of wild events already going down, it’s hard to imagine how it’s going to get even wilder for Subaru in the coming season.

VisionQuest is the last MCU release before Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters in December, and it proved at the end to tie […]
articles.content:
According to Forbes , Marvel reported a production cost of $119.4 million for making VisionQuest . Even after a $25.6 million reimbursement from the United Kingdom, Marvel still spent $93.8 million on the series. Comparatively, Marvel spent $180 million on Captain America: Brave New World , a movie that brought in $415 million worldwide.

'Marvel Reveals It Spent $120 Million Developing Avengers: Doomsday Prequel' via @Forbes by @movieconomics https://t.co/ucQChGizG8

Not only did VisionQuest cost well over $100 million to make, but this is not an anomaly. Marvel has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into its Disney+ shows, offering some great entertainment for fans to watch at home for only the price of the Disney+ subscription. While Marvel is getting nice reimbursements of up to 25.5% from the U.K. on its shows shot over there, each series is still a large investment in something that is almost impossible to measure profits from. The audience for VisionQuest peaked at 3.7 million views globally for the finale.

Marvel’s Moon Knight streaming series cost less than VisionQuest at $95.7 million, while its second series of Loki was higher at $128.4 million. The production included shooting at Hertfordshire’s Hatfield House and White Waltham Airfield in Berkshire, both of which helped earn the tax credits in the U.K. Marvel also paid out $12.7 million to employees working on the series, not including freelancers.

A lot of fans were disappointed when Marvel cancelled Wonder Man after only one season and decided to end Daredevil: Born Again after only three . The big thing that people have to take into account is that these shows cost a lot of money to make. While the total budget of Wonder Man seemed low thanks to the fact that there was almost no superhero action in it, these shows are never cheap, and Disney wants to make sure that the shows make the company money one way or another. Cutting back on the shows is a good way to do so. It also might explain why some ideas that were pitched for shows have moved to possible movies, including Nova and The Champions .
